newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower under bank, utility slump.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower under bank, utility slump.

text.p: A massive slump by two big banks und major utilities pulled Swiss shares down after a restructuring in the Swiss utility sector was announced over the weekend.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) plunged under the psychologically important level of 3,900 points.
Most-active UBS bearer shares plummeted 34 francs to 1,194.
Dealers said opening losses on Wall Street aggravated the market's sluggish performance,although some stocks were buoyed by the firming U.S. dollar.
The SMI ended down 28.5 points, or 0.73 percent, to 3,874.0.
The all-share SPI fell 13.43 points to 2,478.78.
Industrial and power groups Electrowatt and Motor-Columbus led loses.

Electrowatt said last Friday it would spin off its utility business under the name of Watt. CS Holding, which has a stake of 44.9 percent in Electrowatt, will hold an equal stake in Watt as well. Electrowatt fell seven percent to 486 francs.

Motor-Columbus ended down 7.7 percent to 2,520 francs. UBS said on Friday said it was selling two 20 percent stakes in Motor-Columbus to Electricite de France and to RWE for a total sum of 526 million Swiss francs.
UBS said it sold the stakes for 2,600 francs per shares, reducing its stake in Motor-Columbus to 35.6 percent.
Dealers said investors were disappointed that the banks had not sold their respective stakes in Electrowatt and Motor-Columbus, as had been widely speculated earlier this year.

Traders were also disappointed the banks had not merged Electrowatt's utility business and Motor-Columbus in a bigger energy group. "The dream of a Swiss energy holding has not come true for the time being", one trader said.
CS Holding bearers fell 2.9 percent to 134.75 francs.
SMH, ABB, Ciba, Sandoz, Sulzer and Surveillance ended up.
